sprout_scripts.utterance: Three-fourths? That's easy, it's a three and a four! Two numbers.
Wait, is this fraction one thing, or is it really two things, like a 3 and a 4?
I don't get how two numbers stuck together make just one amount.
Maybe this fraction means 3 things AND 4 things? I'm not totally sure.
I'll just say the top number and the bottom number separately, right?
So which one matters more, the top three or the bottom four?
I cut it into 4 pieces, so each piece is 1/4 — the sizes don't matter!
Does it matter if the pieces are different sizes, as long as there are 4?
These pieces look really different, but I still called it 1/4. Is that wrong?
Maybe the pieces need to match somehow? I'm not sure.
Four pieces means fourths, no matter how I cut it, right?
So counting pieces isn't enough — what else do I check?
I think 1/8 is bigger! Eight is way more than four.
Wait, so 1/8 wins because 8 is the bigger number, right?
Hmm, but 8 is more than 4. Doesn't more mean bigger?
Um, maybe 1/8 is bigger? Eight feels like a bigger number to me.
Eight pieces has to beat four pieces, so 1/8 wins, right?
If I had 8 friends instead of 4, wouldn't my share be the bigger one?
1/2 and 2/4 can't be the same — 2/4 has bigger numbers, so it must be more!
Wait, how can two different-looking fractions be the exact same amount?
If the numbers are different, doesn't that mean the fractions are different too?
Maybe they're close but not really equal? I'm not sure.
Bigger top and bottom numbers always means a bigger fraction, right?
So if I make the numbers bigger, does the fraction always grow?
1/4 has to be the biggest — four is such a small bottom number, so the pieces must be huge!
Isn't a smaller bottom number always the winner, no matter what's on top?
I only looked at the bottom numbers. Was I supposed to look at the top too?
Maybe the top number matters sometimes? I'm not sure when.
Smaller bottom number, bigger fraction — that's the rule, right?
So the top number never changes who wins?
That fraction can't be right — the top number can't be bigger than the bottom!
Wait, can a fraction ever be bigger than one whole thing?
I thought fractions were always pieces smaller than one whole.
Maybe that's just a mistake and should really be a whole number instead?
Fractions have to stay under 1, so this one must be wrong, right?
So what does a fraction like that even mean if it's more than a whole pizza?
2/3 of 12? Easy, just divide by the top number: 12 divided by 2 is 6!
Wait, which number tells me how many groups to split into, the top or the bottom?
I keep mixing up which number I'm supposed to divide by.
Maybe I use the bottom number sometimes? I'm not sure when.
The top number is what I divide by, right? That's what I always do.
So the bottom number is just... extra?
1/4 plus 1/4 is 2/8 — just add the tops and add the bottoms!
Wait, do I add the bottom numbers together too, or just the top ones?
Adding fractions feels just like adding regular numbers, top and bottom both.
Maybe the bottom number should stay the same? I'm not totally sure.
Adding is adding — tops together, bottoms together, that's the rule!
So why wouldn't the bottom numbers add up too?
